parsed.main_gap: The key Lemma (every term x has σ(x)=P(x)∩{p≤a₁} good, i.e. large primes are erasable) is asserted with 'details omitted'; this is the entire difficulty of the problem.

errors.description: The central lemma — that the small-prime part of any term is already a good (transversal) set — is stated without any proof. This is the whole substance of the problem; everything else is bookkeeping. An unproved key step of this magnitude cannot be credited.
errors.quote: **Proof.** Induction over the sequence terms in increasing order (standard; details omitted). $\square$

errors.description: The 'surviving hypothesis' section alludes to a repair construction R p^k that is supposed to handle the boundary issue m/p < A, but this construction is never defined or used anywhere in the argument, so the gap in the lemma is not even partially filled.
errors.quote: The construction \(Rp^k\) repairs this boundary issue while preserving exactly the small-prime support; the lemma proves the strengthened hypothesis.

errors.description: Computational checks over 2≤A≤150 are offered in place of the missing argument. Numerical evidence earns no credit, and the text acknowledges it 'only tests' the unproved lemma.
errors.quote: These computations only test the lemma; the argument above proves it independently.

parsed.notes: The reduction framework (goodness, (1), upward closure, L = product of primes ≤ a₁, and the deduction of a_{n+T}=a_n+L valid from n=1) is correct and cleanly written, but it is conditional on an entirely unproved lemma.
